listings.content: Old-style Spanish vacation hotel (CRT TVs in rooms!) is close to the Mar Bella beach. Do note that the hotel is sideways versus the sea, so not all rooms have the same brilliant views.

listings.name: Holiday Inn Express Barcelona City 22@
listings.content: A little run down Holiday Inn Express offers some of the cheapest hotel stays in Barcelona with breakfast included.

listings.name: ibis Barcelona Plaza Glories 22@
listings.content: This is a standard ibis hotel, despite its name not really close to the Plaza Glories. Of note is the fact that no twin rooms are offered, only doubles.

listings.name: NH Diagonal Center
listings.content: The hotel is not really on or near the Diagonal, nor especially central, but all in all offers the usual NH standard in the middle of Sant Marti.

listings.name: Tryp Barcelona Condal Mar
listings.content: In a round modern tower a few blocks north of the Diagonal. Typical Tryp features, including family rooms with foldaway bunk beds.

listings.name: Vincci Bit
listings.content: This unexpectedly stylish hotel is two blocks towards the north from the Diagonal shopping centre. Each floor's corridor is decorated in a different, unusual theme and the cheerful yet tasteful variety of decor makes up for quite small and simple rooms. For thrifty holidaymakers, a Lidl supermarket is around the corner

listings.name: Vincci Maritimo
listings.content: The other Vincci is just as maritime as any other hotel in Sant Marti, as it is actually close to the Diagonal and not the seaside. It is also less adventurous in style, but nonetheless very pleasantly and contemporarily outfitted.

listings.name: AC Hotel Barcelona Forum by Marriott
listings.content: The AC is basically a part of the Convention Centre, towering over its meeting spaces. It features an unusually contemporary design theme for a Marriott-branded property.

listings.name: Barcelo Atenea Mar
listings.content: Right at the Nova Mar Bella beach

listings.name: Barcelona Princess
listings.content: The Princess occupies a tower at the very tip of the Diagonal, boasting great views in all directions and a very metropolitan ambience. The postmodern design mix is enhanced in some rooms appointed with lavishly colourful decorations and patterns by the Spanish apparel brand Desigual.

listings.name: Confortel Barcelona
listings.content: There is nothing really special about the Confortel, apart from really small windows. Rooms are quite sombre and the building is squeezed into one of the blocks at Poblenou.

listings.name: H10 Marina Barcelona
listings.content: A long shot (five blocks) from the actual marina in the Olympic Port, the H10 is a regular midmarket city hotel with a selection of 235 rooms in different sizes and standards. A rooftop terrace with a pool provides a nice overview of Poblenou.

listings.name: Hilton Diagonal Mar Barcelona
listings.content: Adjacent to the Congress Centre and facing the Centro Commercial Diagonal Mar.

listings.name: Melia Barcelona Sky
listings.content: Upscale hotel in Poble Nou neighbourhood. Amenities include free high-speed internet, minibars in all rooms, 24 hour access to the gym, pillow-top mattresses and a pillow menu.

listings.name: Novotel Barcelona City
listings.content: The Novotel boasts a brilliant location on the Diagonal, with excellent views of the neighbouring Agbar Tower, especially from its rooftop pool and terrace. Regular rooms are of the usual old Novotel standard, the upscale categories have been renovated and feature a more modern, edgy design with the use of dark colours.

listings.name: Hotel SB Diagonal Zero
listings.content: 262 rooms and suites, with many having sea views. Amenities include free Wifi, a fitness room, spa, executive floor and a pool with views from the 17th floor.
listings.price: Rooms start from €120 and suites start from €290 (summer)

listings.name: Hotel SB Icaria Barcelona
listings.content: Modern hotel close to the beach and Port Olimpic. Amenities include free Wifi, a solarium with a pool and fitness room. Some rooms are suites with either a study (for business) or a jacuzzi.
listings.price: Rooms start from €150 and suites start from €185 (summer)

listings.name: Silken Diagonal Barcelona
listings.content: Postmodern extravaganza right next door to the Agbar tower.

listings.name: Hotel & Spa Villa Olimpic
listings.content: This hotel with a spa is actually a bit north of the actual Olympic Village. Due to its constrained location within one of the old blocks of Poblenou, the experience there may be less rewarding than in some of the newer hotels.

listings.name: Barcelona Pavilion
listings.content: The Pavilion is one of the emblematic works of Mies van der Rohe and key reference architecture of the twentieth century. The famous German Pavilion was designed for the 1929 Barcelona International Exhibition and reconstructed in 1986 on its original site. Its innovative architectural structure marked a radical change in the layout of space and greatly influenced the development of modern architecture. Furthermore, the Pavilion exhibits the Barcelona Chair, also designed by Mies van der Rohe, along with a bronze reproduction of Georg Kolbe’s sculpture Morning. The Fundació Mies van der Rohe veils for the conservation of the Pavilion.
listings.price: General public €8, student €4; under 16 free; annual subscription €20; entrance fee for groups: groups of more than 15 people with reservation required €6; architectural tour with reservation required €90; discounts: 25% off with Bus Turístic, Barcelona Card and Barcelona City Tour (2022)

listings.name: Caixafòrum
listings.content: Arts & cultural centre.

listings.name: Fundació Joan Miró
listings.content: Treasured museum dedicated to Joan Miró and always has interesting temporary expositions on display.
listings.price: €11 included in the Barcelona Art Passport

listings.name: National Art Museum of Catalonia
listings.content: Has the single best collection of Romanesque art in the world, and a fine Gothic collection as well. Includes the Pantocrator from the Taüll Romanesque church. The building itself is also very beautiful.
listings.price: Adult €12, under 16 or over 65 (EU resident) free, including two visits within 30 days. First Sunday each month is free for everyone. Included in the Barcelona Art Passport
listings.address: Avinguda dels Montanyans, Parc de Montjuic

listings.name: Archaeology Museum of Catalonia
listings.content: Situated on the Montjuic, it exhibits archaeological findings from Catalunia from different periods. Under 16 and 65+ free. €3 for others. Special discounts for other groups.

listings.name: Catalan Ethnographical Museum
listings.content: This museum mainly exhibits exponents, which were imported by Catalan sailors as they explored the new world. Free on the first Sunday each month (11:00 to 15:00)

listings.name: Olympic and Sports Museum Joan Antoni Samaranch
listings.content: The museum displays high-performance sport competitions, recreational sports, sports in general and sports for disabled people. It shows how sport can promote values, educate, innovate and renew. The museum has a sport idols space with outstanding players.

listings.name: Olympic Stadium
listings.content: The stadium and its surroundings built in 1927 and renovated for the 1992 Summer Olympics provides nice architectonic and city views. Since it's not too crowded outside sport events, it's usually a pretty calm place.

listings.name: Plaça d'Espanya
listings.content: Placa d'Espanya was created for the 1929 World Exhibition, on a site once used for public hangings. The fountain in the center of the square is a great attraction and plays music during the summer. Plaça Espanya is located at the base of Montjuic hill.

listings.name: El Poble Espanyol
listings.content: A fake village built in 1929, with replicas of characteristic buildings in Spain (like the Avila walls, the Vall-de-roures town hall, etc.). The village hosts the Fondation Fran Daurel, where you can enjoy an interesting Modern Art collection boasting Miró, Picasso, Tapiès and other, mostly Spanish and Catalan, contemporary artists. The audio tour is very worthwhile there. Also worth seeing - the flamenco show at Tablo de Carmen. You can also step into several of the workshops to see craftsmen at work such as glassblowers and leather workers.

listings.name: Botanical Garden
listings.content: Although a botanic garden had been established in Barcelona as early as 1888, the current gardens date from 1999.

listings.name: Miramar gardens
listings.content: This is where you arrive by a harbour cable car. Marvelous place in the spring, full of roses and fountains. Entrance to the cactus garden is nearby. The Mirador Miramar offers splendid views over the city.

listings.name: The Montjuïc Castle
listings.content: Provides a beautiful panorama view over the rest of the city. The Montjuic Castle is in the Montjuic hill. From the Montjuïc Castle, take the harbor cable car to Barceloneta for more splendid views.

listings.name: Piscina Municipal de Montjuïc
listings.content: In the summer months July and August the outdoor swimming pool is open for public. This pool offers spectacular views over the whole city. The pool is close to the exit from the funicular that departs from metro station Parallel; metro ticket is valid for the funicular.

listings.name: Taberna Blai Tonight
listings.content: A big variety of tapas including cheese, tortillas, seafood and meat options are offered by friendly staff. First one has to choose a plate and a drink. At the end one pays for the number of toothpicks. Cheap drinks attracts a young public.

listings.name: El Sortidor
listings.content: Going back to 1908 the restaurant is known for its anchovies accompanied with good vermouth.

listings.name: Koska Taverna
listings.content: The tapas bar has great drink choices and serves original non traditional food.

listings.name: Quimet & Quimet
listings.content: Lively little bar that serves excellent sandwiches and has a good selection of wines.

listings.name: La tasqueta de Blai
listings.content: The tapas bar is very popular and hence always packed. It offers interesting varieties including sweet dessert ones.

listings.name: Celler Cal Marino
listings.content: Wine bar with lots of local choices plus a great selection of cheeses. They have great suggestions according to personal taste.

listings.name: Gran Bodega Saltó
listings.content: Bar that seems out of the eighties. It is very popular and plays regular concerts.

listings.name: Maumau
listings.content: A chilled out lounge bar with groovy tunes that uses its space to host short film nights, installations and concerts. Their webpage is worth a look for upcoming events and shows in Barcelona.

listings.name: Sala Apolo
listings.content: It is one of the best clubs in town, and the place to be on Monday nights. Concerts every weekend and also during the week.

listings.name: Abirradero
listings.content: Brew pub in the Poble Sec area. A range of dishes to go with the beer.

listings.name: Alberguinn - Sants Youth Hostel
listings.content: Clean, secure and trendy hostel with a team of receptionists that will strive to help you with anything that you may need. The beds are comfortable and a continental breakfast is included. Free computers to use and WIFI. Lockers and bed linen included. Main train station is a few blocks away, as well as 3 metro lines (L1 L3 L5) and an international bus station. Luggage room is also free to use before check-in and after check-out.

listings.name: Hotel Gran Torre Catalunya
listings.content: Avda. Roma, 2-4. Next to Sants Central Station. Restaurant on the 23rd floor, spa, gym. €100.

listings.name: Hotel Medium Prisma 2*
listings.content: Between Sants Station and Plaza Francesc Maciá. 50 rooms, free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Hotel Silken Concordia
listings.content: On a major street. The metro station "Poble Sec" is right across from the hotel. If you prefer to walk you can reach "La Rambla" and all the major atrractions in downtown Barcelona in just 15 minutes. The rooms are spacious, the furniture is almost like new, and the staff are quite friendly.

listings.name: Hotel Medium City 4*
listings.content: Hotel fully renovated, just two minutes walking from the Sants Station. 80 rooms, restaurant, meeting rooms, free Wi-Fi.

listings.name: Tryp Barcelona Apolo Hotel
listings.content: This has to be one of the world's oldest Tryps, and it is so old that it is literally falling apart. The reason why it is still in business is the unparalleled location next to MEtro (pardon the pun) Parallel.

listings.name: hotel Best Auto Hogar Barcelona
listings.content: Nice 4-star hotel of the chain Best.

listings.name: AC Hotel Sants by Marriott
listings.content: AC does the trick by wrapping quite small rooms and limited facilities in modern design in very toned-down hues. Don't expect anything fancy, this is Marriott's lowest-tier brand in Spain. Some of the rooms begin to show dents and cracks after guests failed to properly navigate the narrow bits. The location next to the Sants station is convenient even if a bit sombre.

listings.name: The Urban Suites
listings.content: Holiday Aparments Barcelona: Sant Nicolau 3, 08014. Suites and apartments within walking distance to Spain Square, Sants Station and Montjuic Area. Very well comunicated, through public transport, with the airport and the city center. Free wifi and parking in the same building. Disable friendly.

places.title: Arc de Triomf
places.blurb: The Arc de Triomf, translated: Arch of Victory, is a memorial arch in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.

places.title: Anella Olímpica
places.blurb: Anella Olímpica is an Olympic Park located on the hill of Montjuïc, Barcelona, that was the main site for the 1992 Summer Olympics.

places.title: Ancient synagogue
places.blurb: The Ancient Synagogue of Barcelona is believed to be an ancient Jewish synagogue located in the Jewish quarter of Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.

places.title: Aquarium Barcelona
places.blurb: Aquarium Barcelona is an aquarium located in Port Vell, a harbor in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.

places.title: Alkimia
places.blurb: Alkimia is a Michelin starred restaurant in Barcelona, Spain.

places.title: Sagrada Família
places.blurb: Basílica i Temple Expiatori de la Sagrada Família, or simply Sagrada Família, is a Catholic Basilica in the Eixample district of Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.

places.title: Montjuïc
places.blurb: Montjuïc is a hill in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.

places.title: El Carmel
places.blurb: El Carmel, is a neighbourhood in the district of Horta-Guinardó, in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.

places.title: Palau de la Música Catalana
places.blurb: Palau de la Música Catalana is a concert hall in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.

places.title: Barcelona Cathedral
